To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the dynamic tendency predictor is the best predictor among all the predictors studied, (ii) the dynamic tendency model with different ascending/descending behavior performs best among the dynamic tendency predictors, (iii) the dynamic tendency models with different ascending/descenting behavior perform better than the dynamic tendency model that uses the same ascending/descending parameters, and (iv) the dynamic tendency predictors perform better than the Network Weather Service predictors.

a dynamic tendency predictor with a different ascending and descending tendency behavior performs better than the existing prediction strategies and that this predictor achieves average prediction error that is 36% less than the prediction error achieved by the Network Weather Service predictors.

a dynamic tendency model with separate parameters for ascending and descending trends performs best among the strategies studied, that the best predictor achieves average prediction error reductions of 2% to 55% (36% on average) over the predictors currently used in the NWS system, and that the new predictor is also the fastest.
